A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SketchSplat and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Retained and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction results on ABC-NEF and DTU, runtime measurements, and component and initialization ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds Replica evaluations, depth-estimator comparisons, initialization-noise experiments, filtering analyses, and a NerVE comparison.

M1.justification: The default sketch representation, optimization, and topology operations remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 8 adds an evaluated DepthPro-SN variant that replaces 2DGS depth estimates with DepthPro estimates. The foreground/background sampling explanation is newly disclosed implementation information, without evidence that the default procedure changed.

E1.justification: V2 expands evaluation from ABC-NEF CAD objects and DTU scans to Replica indoor rooms, introducing scene-level coverage in Figure 4. It also evaluates deliberately corrupted initialization conditions. The original ABC-NEF subset and six DTU scans are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds NerVE, with PWL and CAD outputs, to an ABC-NEF comparison against EMAP, EdgeGS, and SketchSplat in Table 10. Comparator membership in the original ABC-NEF and DTU quantitative tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The original evaluation metrics, dataset subsets, normalization, and training budget are retained. Added protocols inject Gaussian noise with sigma values 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10, test filtering at sigma 0.02, and evaluate pretrained NerVE on surface points reconstructed using 2DGS.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and initialization-source ablations, v2 tests alternative depth estimation, sensitivity to initialization noise, and whether filtering becomes useful under noisy initialization. Supplementary Sections 8–10, Tables 6–8, and Figure 6 substantially expand diagnostic evidence about robustness and component behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's Gaussian-noise levels describe experimental perturbations, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All five original quantitative tables retain their numerical values after matching relocations and renumbering. V2 adds DTU/Replica visual and edge-count results and new depth-estimator, noise, filtering, and NerVE results. For example, SketchSplat reports F5 of 87.8 with DepthPro-SN and 58.3 at sigma 0.10, versus the retained default 91.3; these concern different conditions.

T1.justification: The Gaussian representation, rasterization and detector equations, and evaluation-metric definitions remain mathematically unchanged. Metric explanations move from supplementary Section 7 to Section 11. No new theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: direct differentiable parametric-edge optimization, adaptive topology control for compactness, and improved 2D edge detection supporting strong CAD reconstruction. Added experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of depth-scale consistency versus speed, initialization-noise failure conditions, and filtering's usefulness under poor initialization. It also interprets the NerVE comparison as suggesting better robustness and generalization for optimization-based approaches. The original thin-structure, incorrect-supervision, and missed-edge limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project website address, equal foreground/background pixel sampling for the L1 loss, and guidance connecting topology thresholds to scene scale. It documents the 2DGS surface-point input used for NerVE. Existing optimizer, epoch count, hardware, and timing information remains.

R1.justification: DepthPro, Replica, and NerVE are newly cited works. Supplementary Section 14 adds positioning against a feed-forward reconstruction approach, while the main related-work discussion and relationships to existing differentiable reconstruction methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, standardizes SketchSplat terminology, and reorganizes the supplement with a bulleted overview. DTU quantitative discussion moves from the main results section to supplementary Section 13. The main section sequence and most exposition are retained.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, recolors qualitative reconstructions, reduces Figure 3 from five examples to four, and repacks the retained 20 supplementary CAD examples. It adds DTU/Replica and noise figures plus four tables, and relocates the DTU table. Figure 5 numbering is duplicated between the main text and supplement.

improvement.justification: The noise and filtering experiments clarify robustness and explain why filtering showed little benefit in v1's clean-initialization ablation. Additional scene examples, comparison methods, and implementation disclosures strengthen support and reproducibility. The gains are limited by qualitative Replica coverage and the broad generalization inference from one feed-forward comparator; duplicated figure numbering is a small presentation regression.
